summary: VPCE ENI flap causes ephemeral source-port churn and gRPC stream terminations for artifact fetches
description: Customer reports intermittent 5xx and gRPC stream cancellations when the Private deployment pulls model artifacts and metadata. Failures correlate with sudden source-port changes observed from the VPCE service ENI on the tenant VPC. Symptoms look like ephemeral NAT/source-port stickiness breaking long-lived HTTP/2/gRPC sessions used by the artifact fetcher and control-plane heartbeats.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy Private agent into customer VPC connected via VPCE endpoint to Redwood control plane.
Start a model pull that streams artifact layers over HTTP/2 (gRPC) for a large model artifact.
Simulate ENI flap by toggling the VPCE route or invoking reattach (customer observed during route-table changes).
Observe model download progress; watch for gRPC RST/GOAWAY and repeated reconnects.

2026-03-02 09:00 - Eng (Liam): 'Initial theory: ENI/VPCE reassociate is changing source ports and the agent's connection pooling relies on source-port stickiness for HTTP/2 multiplexing. When the port changes we see half-closed streams and the server treats the new connection as a different session leading to RST.'
2026-03-02 11:45 - SRE: 'Observed repeated ephemeral port changes in the pcap correlated exactly with VPCE reattach events. Filed INT-2026 for infra pointer.'
2026-03-03 10:20 - Customer: 'Applying recommended control-plane backoff helped but larger artifacts still fail occasionally.'
investigation_notes: Packet captures show close temporal correlation between VPCE ENI detach/attach events and abrupt client source-port change (NAT mapping lost).
HTTP/2 connections are upgraded to new TCP connections with different 4-tuples causing server-side stream context to be orphaned; server closes the old stream with INTERNAL error after timeout.
Customer's firewall re-inserts asymmetric routing when ENI switches which triggers ephemeral SNAT changes on the VPCE side (confirmed in VPCE flow logs).

Agent uses a connection pool keyed to client 5-tuple; session re-use heuristics didn't survive NAT rebinding, exposing a design assumption in the agent's pool manager for private deployments behind VPCEs.
No TLS certificate errors were present; TLS sessions are re-established but application-layer stream state is not preserved across the port change.
resolution: Workaround: recommend customer enable 'connect-retry-with-new-session' in agent config (forces full stream restart on connection churn) and increase artifact-download parallelism to avoid single-stream bottlenecks. Short term infra mitigation: customer to disable VPCE maintenance that triggers ENI reattachment during active deploy windows and move firewall appliance to inline path with preserved SNAT behavior. Long term fix: engineering to land a change to the agent's connection pool to avoid relying on source-port stability for stream continuation; ticket INT-2978 created for implementation and testing. Customer reported reduced failures after enabling the workaround; monitoring continues.
